title: Timbuktu flourishes as a centre of learning
summary: Mosques, schools and manuscript exchange made Timbuktu a major centre of Islamic scholarship in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Learning was connected to commerce across the Sahara.

claims.text: Mosques, schools and manuscript exchange made Timbuktu a major centre of Islamic scholarship in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Learning was connected to commerce across the Sahara.
A period of intellectual activity, not the foundation date of the city.

Timbuktu broadens the history of knowledge beyond familiar European institutions. Manuscript circulation and teaching can be compared with printing and monastic scholarship elsewhere, without suggesting one common institutional model.
